0.group_name_GPT: Costco Weekly Deal Rapid Product Montage
0.group_des_GPT: This cluster is defined by highly standardized Costco warehouse shopping videos: a graphic-heavy opening with the Costco logo, cartoon avatar, bold Traditional Chinese promotional text, and then a rapid-fire montage of bulk products on pallets, shelves, refrigerated cases, and wine/beer aisles. The closest center examples such as cocowine0205-20251006224824-1399853948027855 and cocowine0205-20250805210251-1341374321358066 show the core pattern most clearly: fast cuts every 1–2 seconds, centered product packaging, bright industrial warehouse lighting, price or discount overlays, minimal human presence, and broad coverage across groceries, meat, snacks, household goods, beverages, and alcohol. Compared with group 4, this group is less personality-led and rarely contains tasting or home-review scenes; the visual logic is catalogue-like, informational, and promotional.
0.group_des_Gemini: This cluster is highly homogenous and characterized by rapid-fire, high-density video montages filmed inside warehouse-style supermarkets (primarily Costco). Represented closely by files like cocowine0205-20251006224824-1399853948027855 and cocowine0205-20250805210251-1341374321358066, these videos function as visual shopping guides. The aesthetic is standardized, utilizing bright industrial lighting, fast cuts (every 1.5 to 2 seconds), static product shelves, and heavy, colorful text overlays displaying price promotions. Human presence is minimized, shifting focus entirely onto product volume and retail-value optimization.

1.group_name_GPT: Tech Presenter Gadget Review and Device Demonstration
1.group_des_GPT: This cluster centers on a male tech presenter explaining smartphones, wearables, chargers, SSDs, AI features, and mobile accessories through studio talk, close-up product handling, screen recordings, and retail-store cutaways. Representative near-center files such as 3ctim-20251020184238-937408758957226, 3ctim-20260106173005-1980985655846717, and 3ctim-20250802223959-4531487993799832 show a recurring structure: the host faces the camera with glasses and a cap, holds or unboxes a device, then cuts to interface demonstrations, side-by-side phone comparisons, camera zoom tests, magnetic accessory tests, or AI feature walkthroughs. The visual style is explanatory and product-spec driven, with many close-ups of ports, buttons, screens, camera modules, boxes, and on-screen menus. It differs from group 7 because products are mainly consumer electronics rather than beauty or skincare, and differs from group 6 because it is presenter-led review content rather than multi-person podcast conversation.
1.group_des_Gemini: This group is defined by consumer electronics reviews dominated by a middle-aged male host (e.g., Tim in 3ctim-20251020184238-937408758957226 and 3ctim-20260106173005-1980985655846717). The content emphasizes functional demonstrations of smartphones, smartwatches, and external SSDs. Visually, it transitions between professional studio spaces with solid-color backdrops and retail environments. It relies on macro shots of device profiles, camera zoom tests, screen recordings of user interfaces, and graphic specification overlays, framing the host as a trusted tech utility expert.

2.group_name_GPT: Selfie Persona Monologue and Flirtatious Short Performance
2.group_des_GPT: This cluster features short, intimate, single-person videos dominated by a young woman speaking or posing directly to the camera in bedrooms, domestic interiors, or casual outdoor settings. The closest examples, including 0_shufen-20250905070450-1461416632060937, 0_shufen-20250904140410-1447376430235569, and 0_shufen-20250911084048-896432156127037, emphasize direct eye contact, facial expressions, playful gestures, teasing poses, simple static or handheld selfie framing, and minimal narrative environment. Many clips show outfit-focused or body-aware presentation, light comedy, coughing or pointing gestures, leaning toward the lens, hair adjustment, smiling, pouting, or short punchline delivery. Unlike group 7, these videos are generally not structured around product demonstration or before/after proof; unlike group 5, they are not group activity or family entertainment. The core is personal presence, attractiveness, micro-performance, and direct parasocial address.
2.group_des_Gemini: Characterized by close-up, portrait-oriented selfie videos, this cluster relies on direct face-to-face communication to cultivate high parasocial intimacy. Representative videos like 0_shufen-20250905070450-1461416632060937 and 0_shufen-20250904140410-1447376430235569 feature a young female creator in private domestic settings like bedrooms. The visual style is marked by subtle, playful, or teasing facial expressions, micro-actions (e.g., touching the cheek, playing with hair), and natural handheld camera shakes, prioritizing emotional connection over structured tutorials.

3.group_name_GPT: Food Tasting, Mukbang, Restaurant Visit, and Home Cooking
3.group_des_GPT: This cluster is visually organized around food as the central object: eating, cooking, restaurant visits, street food, bakery purchases, noodles, stews, snacks, raw seafood, dumplings, rice dishes, and desserts. Near-center examples such as khshu_-20251119165209-25620650587562329, khshu_-20260103064142-1233342455437429, and 602avenue-20250729124534-904960372274534 show the key pattern: a creator presents food, cuts to preparation or restaurant context, then uses close-ups of texture, steam, cheese pulls, sauce, fillings, noodles, or bites, followed by expressive tasting reactions. This group includes travel food exploration, home recipe assembly, takeout mukbangs, and restaurant review visuals. It differs from group 0 because products are consumed and evaluated rather than merely listed as deals, and differs from group 4 because the food is not specifically framed as a Costco product discovery followed by a two-person home test.
3.group_des_Gemini: This cluster revolves around the somatic experience of eating, food hunting, and restaurant exploration. Closely aligned with files like khshu_-20251119165209-25620650587562329 and khshu_-20260103064142-1233342455437429, the visual narrative follows hosts visiting cafes, local eateries, and traditional restaurants. The visual grammar focuses on the sensory textures of food, utilizing steaming close-ups of dishes (e.g., Nasi Lemak, soup dumplings, or bakery items) and exaggerated facial expressions of pleasure and critique during tasting, set against bustling dining backdrops.

4.group_name_GPT: Costco Personality-Led Product Discovery and Home Taste Test
4.group_des_GPT: This cluster is centered on female creators personally presenting one Costco product in the warehouse, then often moving to a home setting for unboxing, cooking, tasting, or texture review with another woman. The closest examples, such as cocowine0205-20250806233029-1583100049473544, cocowine0205-20250804015918-1455352252714125, cocowine0205-20250810160505-4575375356029901, and cocowine0205-20250706162533-2111054489629804, show a strong template: a young woman in a Costco aisle or freezer section holds a featured item, points to packaging or price tags, uses energetic facial expressions and variety-style captions, then cuts to a domestic table where two women open, cook, tear apart, taste, and react. Products include shrimp, fruit cakes, bread, crab salad sandwiches, cherries, pastries, dumplings, salads, snacks, and themed items. Compared with group 0, this group is much more creator-centered, slower, and experiential; compared with group 3, it is specifically anchored in Costco discovery and packaged-product evaluation.
4.group_name_Gemini: Two-Host Domestic Food Unboxing & Comedic Tasting
4.group_des_Gemini: This group features a structured narrative arc: a female creator first browses bulk products in a retail warehouse, then transitions to a cozy domestic interior to unbox, prepare, and taste the food alongside a companion. Highly represented by cocowine0205-20250806233029-1583100049473544 and cocowine0205-20250804015918-1455352252714125, the style leans into variety-show aesthetics, featuring dual reactions, exaggerated comedic expressions of taste, close-ups of food being pulled apart, and bright, warm home lighting that emphasizes friendship.

The cinematography utilizes active tracking shots, playful physical challenges (e.g., sports, dance routines), and kids interacting with games, cultivating a sense of comedic chaos and collective celebration.

6.group_des_GPT: This cluster consists of seated talk-show or podcast-style content in studio environments with microphones, headphones, couches, figurine shelves, curtains, and repeated cuts among speakers. Close examples such as yga0721-20250630124033-1085900153665565, yga0721-20260112023602-1159441849602125, and yga0721-20250503053514-1415983970173746 show the main grammar: a host or guests speak into professional microphones, react with laughter, gesture while telling stories, and are intercut with a recurring oversized masked character or other participants. Backgrounds often include anime figurines, designer toys, framed illustrations, leather sofas, and studio lighting. The defining visual trait is conversational reaction editing rather than product demonstration, travel, or eating. Compared with group 5, action is mostly seated and verbal; compared with group 1, the format is entertainment discussion rather than informational tech review.

7.group_name_GPT: Beauty, Skincare, Makeup, and Personal Care Demonstration Ads
7.group_des_GPT: This cluster focuses on beauty and personal-care routines, often with problem-solution storytelling, application close-ups, texture demonstrations, before/after comparisons, and promotional product displays. The closest examples include 602avenue-20251004225909-1713898022917032, 2uncle987-20250604213238-3495084214001157, and 2uncle987-20250601095023-25611298551845742, where creators show smudged makeup, skin texture, dark spots, dullness, irritation, dandruff, hair frizz, or hygiene concerns, then apply cleansers, serums, creams, toners, masks, hair dye, shampoo, sanitizer, or cosmetics. Visuals frequently include bathroom sinks, bright home studios, macro shots of foam, serum droplets, foundation, lip tint, scalp, hair roots, or skin texture, and final product bundles with sales overlays. It differs from group 2 because the creator’s face and body are used to demonstrate a product transformation, and differs from group 1 because the review object is beauty or health-care texture and efficacy rather than electronic function.
7.group_des_Gemini: This cluster focuses on personal grooming, beauty, and cosmetic routines. Closely represented by 602avenue-20251004225909-1713898022917032 and 2uncle987-20250604213238-3495084214001157, the content is highly instructional, filmed in bathrooms or bedrooms showing the application of skincare serums, face masks, hair dyes, or cosmetics. It relies on split-screen Before & After skin comparisons, macro close-ups of product textures (foams, creams), and extreme close-ups of skin application, emphasizing scientific efficacy and transformation.
